html:
The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, a cartel of oil-producing states. It was founded in Baghdad on 14 September 1960 by Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela.

At the time a handful of Western companies, the "Seven Sisters", controlled most of the world's oil. Several grew out of Standard Oil, Royal Dutch Shell and the Anglo-Persian Oil Company. They set the prices and paid the producing countries a share. When they cut prices in 1959 and 1960 without asking, Venezuela and Saudi Arabia led the move to form a common front. The headquarters moved to Vienna in 1965.

In the 1970s OPEC members took control of their oil. Many nationalised the companies working in their lands, as Saudi Arabia did step by step with Aramco. The 1973 Arab oil embargo quadrupled prices, and the Iranian Revolution of 1979 sent them up again. Money flowed to the Gulf, and with it millions of migrant workers, many from South Asia, such as the workers from Kerala.

OPEC's grip has weakened as other producers grew. Since 2016 it has coordinated with Russia and others as "OPEC+". Its members still hold most of the world's proven oil reserves.
sum: The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, a cartel of oil-producing states. It was founded in Baghdad on 14 September 1960 by Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela.
